transcript:
Header:
Date: 2025-05-07
Start time: 16:00 PDT
Duration: 55 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Ethan (Redwood SE), Liam (ZenithTech), Sofia (ZenithTech), Priya (ZenithTech)
Artifacts referenced: co-sell deck (zenith-redwood-co-sell-05.pdf), pricing sheet (zenith-pricing-v2.xlsx), security pack (redwood-security-pack.pdf)

Summary: quick partner pipeline review focused on 3 joint opps, alignment on who owns which accounts for outreach, initial perf benchmarking ask for two proof points, and confirmation of legal/contract steps for co-sell. Some audio/transcription artifacts present (product names sometimes garbled).

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya: Ok hey everyone, thanks for carving out time. this is Maya from Redwood, I'm the AE on the co-sell. with me is Ethan, our solutions engineer.
[00:12] Ethan: hi all, Ethan Ross, SE. I'll be handling the perf & security bits.
[00:18] Liam: Liam Chen, Head of Partnerships at ZenithTech, great to see you both.
[00:22] Sofia: Sofia Morales, I run enterprise sales, I'll be coordinating the rep motions.
[00:26] Priya: Priya Kapoor, solutions architect, I'll own technical intake.
[00:30] Maya: cool, agenda—quick pipeline run through, discuss two technical asks (benchmarking + SSO/KMS questions), and align on next steps and timeline. Sound good?
[00:38] Liam: yep, go for it.

[00:45] Maya: first up, three deals we have listed as joint opps. One is "AcmeFin" (stage: discovery), second is "BlueHarbor" (stage: evaluation) and third is "OrbitWare" (early scoping). we sent the joint deck last week. any updates from your side?
[01:05] Sofia: AcmeFin is priority for us, Liam's team already intro'd to their cloud infra lead, they're sensitive about data residency—want to confirm if Redwood can support private deployment or VPC peering for a bank/regulatory environment.
[01:25] Ethan: right, for that use case we typically propose Redwood Private (VPC). There's an on-prem option too but that has longer lead time. our Private offering supports customer-managed VPC and KMS integrations.
[01:39] Priya: couple clarifying q's — what's the expected latency SLO if they have a 100ms target for small chat prompts? and how does kv cache behave in a multi-tenant config?
[01:55] Ethan: good q. for 100ms you're probably looking at dedicated capacity and model selection — we can hit sub-100 on a 16k context with the right kernel config but it's model dependent. and the KV cache (sometimes the transcription shows KV cash, haha) is per-tenant on Dedicated and Private; on Hosted we have prefix caching but it's shared so you get the benefit of caching without tenant-level isolation unless you go Private/Dedicated.
[02:20] Maya: I'll flag that in the deck for AcmeFin. on the legal front Acme asked about data retention and SOC 2; we have a SOC 2 Type II report and can provide it.
[02:32] Liam: great, please send that. also, Acme asked whether we can appear as co-sell partner on the initial intro email—do you have a co-sell intro template?
[02:41] Maya: yes we do, I'll send the template and recommended playbook.

[02:50] Maya: next deal, BlueHarbor: this is a mid-market SaaS using embeddings/ search. Sofia, you mentioned they care about token cost.
[02:59] Sofia: yep, they're elastic usage, cost sensitivity. we wanted to know how Redwood's batching and quantization recommendation could cut costs compared to Anthropic and OpenAI options.
[03:12] Ethan: batching, prefix caching and quantization profiles are the key levers. in our experience, for retrieval-heavy workloads you can see 30-50% token cost reduction vs unoptimized endpoints; depends on sequence length distribution. we can run a quick bench to show cost per 1M tokens on a comparable model.
[03:31] Priya: also please clarify if those savings affect latency in a way that would break the user's SLA.
[03:36] Ethan: there is a tradeoff. batching helps cost but can add tens of ms; smart routing plus autoscaling keeps tail latency predictable. we'll bake in latency numbers in the benchmark.

[03:50] Maya: third opportunity OrbitWare—this one is interesting, they run large-context summarization. they asked about model rollouts and fallback to smaller models during peak.
[03:59] Ethan: we support rollout policies with automatic fallback to compatible model variants; it's baked into the routing layer. example: if GPU capacity is constrained we'll fallback from a 8-bit quantized llama variant to a smaller ver that still meets quality thresholds.
[04:15] Liam: perfect. that helps the sales story.

[04:22] Maya: ok technical ask #1 — benchmarking. Priya, you said you could provide a representative prompt set?
[04:29] Priya: yes, I'll upload samples to the shared folder by Monday. they'd be a mix of long-context and short queries, about 200 prompts.
[04:36] Ethan: great, with that we can run two short benchmarks: one targeting latency SLOs (p95) and one cost/run tradeoffs. we'll deliver a short report with numbers and recommended config.
[04:47] Maya: timeline for that?
[04:49] Ethan: if we get prompts by 2025-05-12 we can run labs and share results by 2025-05-14.
[04:56] Priya: sounds good.

[05:02] Maya: technical ask #2 — security & compliance. Acme and BlueHarbor asked about encryption at rest/in transit and KMS.
[05:12] Ethan: we support customer-managed keys via KMS/HSM in Private deployments; hosted API uses Redwood-managed keys but we offer envelope encryption and dedicated customer key options for enterprise tiers. we'll attach the redwood-security-pack.pdf.
[05:27] Sofia: any gaps for SAML SSO and RBAC for admins? our reps want to know if the console supports fine-grained roles.
[05:35] Ethan: console supports SAML SSO, SCIM provisioning, and RBAC down to team and route levels. we can demo role mapping in a follow-up.

[05:45] Liam: from a GTM standpoint, we want to agree on who owns intro emails and which logos we can use. also co-marketing funds?
[05:53] Maya: for logos, we'll provide a short legal addendum for co-marketing. on co-marketing funds we typically have a small MDF for initial joint webinars — we can propose an amount once we see the pipeline.
[06:06] Liam: ok good.

[06:10] Maya: quick note — a few of our prior partner calls had some confusion around product names; sometimes Redwood Dedicated appeared as "Redwood Dedcated" in notes. just wanted to call out potential transcription inconsistencies.
[06:22] everyone: laugh / agree

[06:30] Maya: let's run through the three opps in a little more detail — AcmeFin: Sofia, can you remind us of timeline?
[06:36] Sofia: AcmeFin wants a POC within 6 weeks, decision by end of Q3. main blockers: security review and infra proof.
[06:45] Maya: ok so immediate next steps: send SOC 2 + security pack, share co-sell intro template, Priya to upload prompts, Ethan to run bench after prompts in the week of 5/12.
[06:58] Liam: noted.

[07:05] Maya: BlueHarbor — we need a cost comparison vs Anthropic & OpenAI. Ethan, you'll own the bench?
[07:11] Ethan: yes. also we'll include quantization profile recommendations; might suggest a 4-bit quantized variant for cost/quality balance.
[07:19] Priya: any constraints on inference hardware? they'd likely ask about GPUs; be explicit about supported SKUs.
[07:25] Ethan: we'll include supported GPU SKUs in the report and map them to perf numbers.

[07:32] Maya: OrbitWare — they asked about canary rollouts and fallback. we'll send a short doc on rollout policies and a sample policy.
[07:41] Liam: can you also share a sample SLA language for Dedicated?
[07:45] Maya: yes, we'll include the SLA excerpt.

[07:50] Sofia: one more commercial question — revenue split model for co-sell. do you do margin-based splits or referral fees?
[07:58] Maya: we generally do referral/reseller agreements varying by region; for larger deals we can discuss revenue share. I'll loop in legal to draft a starter term sheet.

[08:09] Liam: good.

[08:14] -- (fast forward through a few clarifying exchanges, timestamps jump) --
[20:12] Priya: a quick nit — for the long-context summarization use case, what's your recommended model family?
[20:18] Ethan: for long context we recommend the latest Llama-derived variants we verified; we'll call out exact model names in the bench. note transcription often masks model names, so we'll be explicit in the doc.
[20:30] Priya: perfect.

[32:05] Sofia: about the co-marketing webinar — what's the expected joint exec involvement? we can get a product SA and a rep, do you want an exec?
[32:13] Maya: exec presence helps for enterprise doors, but for initial pipeline building we usually do product SA + partner rep + customer success conversation. we can scale up if we hit mid-market targets.

[38:40] Ethan: technical note — if you want a private deployment for AcmeFin, lead time is usually 6–8 weeks for onboarding + security review; Dedicated can be faster if you already have committed SKUs in cloud.

[42:00] Liam: any red flags on the dependency side? legal/IP?
[42:06] Maya: main ones are data residency and audit logs — both covered by our Private offering. we'll provide examples of audit log exports.

[49:10] Sofia: ok commercial: once we have bench numbers and security pack we'll prepare an initial proposal.
[49:18] Maya: sounds good.

[49:25] Maya: recap / next steps — I'll run through them: 1) Maya to send co-sell pricing & template + SOC 2 + security pack by 2025-05-10; 2) Priya to upload prompt set by 2025-05-12; 3) Ethan to run benchmarks and share report by 2025-05-14; 4) Liam to confirm target accounts and list of logos by 2025-05-15; 5) schedule a follow-up call (pipeline sync + bench review) for the week of 2025-05-19. any objections?
[49:55] Liam: none.
[49:57] Sofia: ok good.
[50:00] Priya: fine.

[50:05] Maya: last few logistics: I'll attach the co-sell deck and pricing in the follow-up email. look out for a calendar invite for the bench review.
[50:14] Ethan: I'll include a short appendix showing latency vs quantization tradeoffs.

[50:20] Liam: thanks all.
[50:22] Maya: thanks everyone, talk soon.
[50:24] Meeting ends

Notes: transcription shows occasional mis-hearings ("KV cash" instead of "KV cache", "Redwood Dedcated"), speaker labels mostly accurate. References to docs are placeholders; actual files to be shared via SFDC/drive.

Explicit next steps (as discussed):
- Redwood: send SOC2/security pack, co-sell template, pricing (due 2025-05-10)
- ZenithTech: provide prompts and success criteria (due 2025-05-12), confirm logo list (due 2025-05-15)
- Redwood SE: run benchmarks and share results (due 2025-05-14)

End of transcript.
